The main takeaway from our work is that

the human perception of scatter plot similarity can be reliably modelled by using a small set of perceptually meaningful features, which can then be used for the analysis of large sets of scatter plot representations.

human observers can reliably group scatter plot representations into similarity clusters, that these groups have perceptually meaningful features, and that these features are not reliably captured by scagnostics.

there are a number of perceptual concepts that are important for scatter plot similarity, which can be used as guidelines for the design of scatter plot similarity algorithms, or as a basis for a similarity model.
